jobs.title: Software Quality Engineer
jobs.description: Zipliens is a leading lien resolution company that specializes in streamlining the lien process for personal injury law firms. Our work helps law firms operate more efficiently and helps the injured people they serve access settlement funds more quickly and accurately. We are looking for a quality engineer who is passionate about building the testing and evaluation that keeps complex, data\-heavy products working correctly at scale. Zipliens is looking for a Quality Engineer to join our team and own quality for a product area within the applications we build for the legal industry. After several years of high growth, Zipliens has become a leader in lien resolution, a process required in most personal injury settlements. The software we build supports that work, so the quality of what we ship has a clear, real\-world impact on law firms and the people they represent. We're scaling engineering significantly this year, and quality engineering is growing along with it. QA at Zipliens is embedded in the engineering teams and combines exploratory testing with automation. You'd own quality for a feature or product area, including the test strategy, the automation behind it, and the release sign\-off for that area. You'll have established patterns and existing test suites to work from, and you'll help improve them as the team grows. We also build with AI as a first\-class part of the workflow, and that applies to testing as much as to development. Our product uses LLMs to extract structure from medical records and lien correspondence, so evaluating non\-deterministic output is a regular part of the job. We also use agentic coding tools and internal skills and harnesses we've written ourselves to build and maintain automation, and you'd be expected to use those tools well, review what they produce, and help improve them. **Requirements**### **Responsibilities:** * Own quality for a feature or product area, including the risk\-based test strategy, the regression scope, and the release sign\-off for that area. * Build and maintain the automated test suites for your area and keep them integrated with CI. When tests fail or become flaky, you'll troubleshoot them and fix the underlying cause. * Run exploratory testing against the lien workflow and develop a detailed understanding of the applications your team owns, including their risk areas and failure modes. * Test our LLM\-based features. This includes building the evaluation suite for a feature, setting acceptance thresholds with product (for example, precision and recall targets for extraction), checking LLM\-judge agreement against human labels, and adding adversarial and prompt\-injection cases. * Use agentic coding tools to build and maintain automation, and review AI\-generated tests before they merge. * Join refinement early enough to shape Acceptance Criteria with the Product Owner, flag testability gaps before development starts, and recommend coverage and risk priorities for your area. * Shepherd defects for your area from triage through resolution, writing clear, reproducible reports that engineers can act on. * Work directly with the engineers on your team day to day. QA at Zipliens is embedded in the engineering teams rather than run as a separate function. ### **Qualifications:** * 3\+ years on a QA or software development team, including experience owning test coverage for a feature or product area. * Strong skills in at least one of exploratory testing and test design, test automation and infrastructure, or AI/LLM evaluation, with working proficiency in a second. We don't expect the same depth in all three. * Hands\-on experience building and maintaining automated test suites in a modern framework (Playwright, Cypress, pytest, or similar), including diagnosing flaky tests and fixing their root causes. * Comfortable reading and writing code. Our backend is Python/Django and our frontend is React, and you should be able to read a change in either and understand what it affects and what it puts at risk. * Experience integrating tests into CI pipelines and deciding which checks should gate a merge or a deploy. * Strong SQL. Much of what we test lives in PostgreSQL, and verifying a workflow often means verifying the data it produced as well as what the UI shows. * Hands\-on experience testing LLM or ML features, whether in production or through prototypes and experimentation: building golden datasets, measuring output quality, and understanding how these systems fail. * Experience using or experimenting with agentic coding tools, and good judgment about when their output needs a closer look. * Clear written communication. You'll be writing defect reports, test plans, and release sign\-offs for engineers and product, and explaining risk to non\-technical stakeholders. ### **Nice to Have:** * Experience testing document processing or extraction from unstructured data. * Experience testing third\-party integrations, especially where the counterparty's documentation isn't solid and you need contract tests, sandboxes, or recorded fixtures to work around it. * Familiarity with AWS and Kubernetes. jobs.title: Lead/ Senior Machine Learning Scientist, Integrative Phenotyping
jobs.description: **The Opportunity** ------------------- insitro is a physical AI company dedicated to unlocking causal human biology and accelerating the delivery of better medicines to patients. Our unique Virtual Human™ platform identifies novel, high\-impact genetic intervention points, which our TherML™ platform translates into therapeutics—whether small molecules, biologics, or oligos. With multiple programs in metabolic disease and neuroscience advancing toward the clinic, and our first IND submission slated for the second half of this year, we are at a pivotal inflection point. As a **Lead/ Senior Machine Learning Scientist** on the Integrative Phenotyping team, you will develop, productionize, and deploy cutting\-edge ML approaches to build precise phenotypes from large\-scale multimodal datasets — clinical imaging, electronic health records, longitudinal outcomes, biomarkers, and multi\-omic readouts — and use them to understand patient state, predict clinical endpoints, and identify therapeutic targets. You’ll work alongside machine learning scientists, statistical geneticists, life scientists, software engineers, and clinicians, and your expertise will shape how the company builds rigorous ML on complex human data. Based in South San Francisco, this position **reports directly to the Head of Integrative Phenotyping** and offers an **in\-person hybrid schedule of three days per week**. **Responsibilities** -------------------- **ML Methods \& Platform** * **Build Precise Phenotypes:** Develop and deploy ML methods that extract biological insight from complex, high\-dimensional human cohort data such as MRI and functional genomics. * **Model Patient State:** Develop models that characterize patient state and predict outcomes and clinical endpoints from multimodal data including clinical imaging, EHRs, longitudinal outcomes, biomarkers, and multi\-omic readouts. * **Set the Bar:** Ensure modeling strategies are rigorous, effective, and aligned with best practices in the field. * **Engineer Reusable Components:** Build robust, reusable platform components in partnership with the software engineering team. **Target Discovery \& Translation** * **Integrate Causal Evidence:** Combine causal, multimodal analyses across diverse phenotypic readouts to select better therapeutic targets. * **Biomarkers \& Endpoints:** Partner with Therapeutic Area and Clinical Development colleagues to develop new biomarkers for patient selection and clinical endpoints. * **Connect Genetics to Phenotypes:** Work with the Statistical Genetics team to associate human genetics with ML\-derived phenotypes. **About You** ------------- **Experience \& Qualifications** * **Proven Tenure:** PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or 5\+ years of equivalent applied ML research experience. * **Modern ML Expertise:** Hands\-on experience developing and deploying state\-of\-the\-art ML methods, including multimodal techniques, to extract clinically relevant signals from complex data. * **Clinical Data Depth:** Experience with several of: clinical imaging (e.g., MRI, DEXA, CT, echocardiography), clinical records (e.g., EHRs, medications, outcomes), physiological recordings (e.g., EEG, ECG), or biobank\-scale human genetic data. * **Multimodal Experience:** Experience with high\-content modalities such as single\-cell or bulk omics, genetic perturbation screening, spatial proteomics, or pooled optical screening. * **Publication Record:** Meaningful, high\-quality contributions in ML, ML for health, computational biology, or biomedical venues. * **Engineering Fluency:** Strong Python in a cloud environment and modern deep learning frameworks, with a track record of reusable, tested, version\-controlled ML code. **Core Competencies** * **End\-to\-End Delivery:** You work with other ML scientists and engineers to take a real\-world problem from sourcing and qualifying training data through model design, testing, and benchmarking. * **Cross\-Functional Translator:** You collaborate well with statistical geneticists, life scientists, software engineers, and clinicians, and can make ML results legible to each. * **Biology\-Curious:** You want to understand the physiology behind the data, and prior exposure to cardiovascular disease, neuroscience, or metabolism is a plus. **Compensation \& Benefits at insitro** --------------------------------------- Our target starting salary for successful US\-based applicants for this role is **$183,000 \- $224,000**. To determine starting pay, we consider multiple job\-related factors including a candidate's skills, education and experience, market demand, business needs, and internal parity. We may also adjust this range in the future based on market data. This role is eligible for participation in our Annual Performance Bonus Plan (based on company targets by role level and annual company performance) and our Equity Incentive Plan, subject to the terms of those plans and associated policies. In addition, insitro also provides our employees: * 401(k) plan with employer matching for contributions * Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as mental health and well\-being support * Open, flexible vacation policy * Paid parental leave of at least 16 weeks to support parents who give birth, and 10 weeks for a new parent (inclusive of birth, adoption, fostering, etc) * Quarterly budget for books and online courses for self\-development * New hire stipend for home office setup * Monthly cell phone \& internet stipend * Access to free onsite baristas and daily lunch for employees who are either onsite or hybrid * Access to a free commuter bus network that provides transport to and from our South San Francisco HQ from locations all around the Bay Area insitro is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status. We believe diversity, equity, and inclusion need to be at the foundation of our culture. We work hard to bring together diverse teams–grounded in a wide range of expertise and life experiences–and work even harder to ensure those teams thrive in inclusive, growth\-oriented environments supported by equitable company and team practices. All candidates can expect equitable treatment, respect, and fairness throughout the interview process. \#LI\-Onsite *Please be aware of recruitment scams: we never request payments, all recruitment communications are from @**insitro.com**, and if in doubt, contact us at* *info@insitro.com**.* **About insitro** insitro is a drug discovery and development company using machine learning (ML) and data at scale to decode biology for transformative medicines. At the core of insitro’s approach is the convergence of in\-house generated multi\-modal cellular data and high\-content phenotypic human cohort data. We rely on these data to develop ML\-driven, predictive disease models that uncover underlying biologic state and elucidate critical drivers of disease. These powerful models rely on extensive biological and computational infrastructure and allow insitro to advance novel targets and patient biomarkers, design therapeutics and inform clinical strategy. insitro is advancing a wholly owned and partnered pipeline of insights and therapeutics in neuroscience and metabolism. Since launching in 2018, insitro has raised over $700 million from top tech, biotech and crossover investors, and from collaborations with pharmaceutical partners. For more information on insitro, please visit www.insitro.com.

jobs.title: Senior Android Engineer - Identity & Access Management
jobs.description: ### **ABOUT onX** We’re a team of builders, adventurers, and risk takers using technology to help people confidently explore the outdoors. Driven by our mission to awaken the adventurer inside everyone, we build products that optimize every outdoor experience and inspire confidence to get out and go further. We’re a high\-growth tech company. The pace is fast, the work takes grit, and ambiguity is part of the job. As the world changes around us, we adapt \- continuously evolving how we build, prioritize, and deliver. Our business moves quickly, and there’s real opportunity to shape what we build next. Each of our verticals \- Hunt, Offroad, Backcountry, and Fish \- is at a different stage of maturity, which means the challenges you encounter and the impact you have will vary depending on where you sit and what the business needs most. We operate with an experimentation mindset, continually iterating and improving how we solve problems. We expect our people to use the latest tooling, including AI, thoughtfully and responsibly, pairing human judgment with technology to increase quality, speed, and impact. Our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access. ### **ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY** onX is seeking a Senior Android Engineer who will contribute to meaningful, real\-world outcomes that have a lasting impact for customers and the business. In this role, as part of the Identity \& Access Management (IAM) team, you’ll focus on owning the Android client libraries that power authentication, sessions and feature access across every onX app , and the pipeline for sign\-ups and entitlements. You’ll be supporting secure, reliable access to onX Hunt, Offroad, Fish and Backcountry for millions of hunters, anglers and outdoor enthusiasts, including when they’re far from a cell signal. You’ll take ownership of your work, collaborate closely with partners across the organization, and help move initiatives forward in an environment where priorities evolve, learning is celebrated, and you’re encouraged to keep stretching your skills. This role will report to a Software Engineering Manager III. ### **WHAT YOU'LL DO** ***Essential Job Duties \& Functions*** * **Own the platform.** You’ll own onX’s Android identity, subscription, and feature\-access libraries: shared Kotlin modules consumed by every onX Android app. You’ll set their technical direction, decide which patterns to keep and which to replace, and see changes through to production. You’ll co\-own the API contracts with backend and push for changes when needed. * **Make auth dependable in the field.** You’ll harden token refresh and session lifecycle, apply coroutines and structured concurrency correctly, and handle network loss and process death gracefully so users stay signed in when they need the app most. * **See what’s happening.** You’ll build client\-side observability for identity flows so the team can see auth health by device, OS version and app, then use that data to find and fix problems before customers report them. * **Champion both directions.** You’ll represent Android in IAM design work (account management, session management, passkeys, one\-time passwords, entitlements and bundling) and represent IAM in the Android codebase, partnering with backend engineers, Android platform leads and product teams across our apps. You’ll push for new capabilities when the current ones aren’t enough. * **Work with your iOS counterpart.** You’ll be partnered on the team with an iOS counterpart to keep identity and entitlement behavior consistent: shared specs, shared test cases, and joint design docs. * **Raise the bar.** You’ll grow the team’s client expertise through code review, documentation and mentoring, including backend engineers who contribute to client code. You’ll identify the next problems worth solving, write the design doc, align stakeholders, and drive it through rollout across apps. * **Adopt new technologies.** You’ll look for opportunities to embed AI as a repeatable co\-pilot in daily workflows by integrating experimentation into real work, and continuously refining its use with sound judgment and validation. * **Support for uptime and availability.** You’ll join the team\-based oncall rotation for the Identity team. While this does not require strong backend expertise, you may occasionally need to follow a runbook or escalate depending on the situation. ### **WHAT YOU’LL BRING** * Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience. * Six or more years of professional software development experience, with building and shipping production Android apps in Kotlin as a primary focus for at least three of those years, is required. * Deep knowledge of Kotlin, coroutines and Flow, and experience diagnosing race conditions, lifecycle and threading issues in production apps. * Experience building and maintaining a  n Bozeman and Missoula, MT, along with virtual workforce “Basecamps” in Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Kalispell, MT; Minneapolis, MN; Portland, OR; Salt Lake City, UT; and Seattle, WA. Basecamps are not physical offices; they are geographic hubs made up of remote employees who live within a 60\-mile radius of the city center, creating opportunities for local connection and collaboration. We have a strong preference for hiring candidates who live near one of our offices or within a Basecamp, and we prioritize candidates in these locations first. Candidates who live elsewhere in the U.S. may still be considered, provided they reside in a state where onX is currently able to employ team members. At this time, we are **NOT** able to employ individuals whose primary work location is in: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia (D.C.), Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, South Dakota, West Virginia, and Wyoming. ### **HOW YOU’LL BE COMPENSATED** onX is committed to compensating all employees fairly and equitably for their contributions. For this position, we are open to considering candidates ranging in two levels (level II and level III). Spanning these levels, applicants can expect to make between $146,000 to $182,000 upon hire. The pay range will vary based on experience, skills, certifications, and education among other factors as required in the job description. In addition, full\-time onX employees are eligible for a grant of common share options with a vesting schedule and a potential annual bonus of 10% based on company performance. ### **WHAT WE’RE OFFERING YOU** * Competitive salaries, annual bonuses, equity, and opportunities for growth * Comprehensive health benefits, including a no\-monthly\-cost medical plan * Paid parental leave of 13 weeks for birthing parents and 5 weeks for non\-birthing parents * 401k matching at 100% for the first 3% you save and 50% from 3\-5% * Company\-wide outdoor adventures and amazing outdoor industry perks * Annual “Get Out, Get Active” funds to fuel your active lifestyle * Flexible time away package that includes PTO, STO, VTO, and paid holidays ### **PERFORMANCE ESSENTIALS** In this role, success is driven by cognitive abilities such as concentration and problem\-solving, essential for our computer\-centric tasks. onX will explore reasonable accommodations to ensure that individuals with diverse abilities can fully engage in and contribute to the essential physical and mental functions of the job. If you need assistance or accommodation, please contact us at PC@onxmaps.com. **Position open until filled.** **\#LI\-Remote** **At onX, we believe that unique perspectives make us stronger.** By bringing together people with different experiences, ideas, and viewpoints, we fuel innovation and move closer to our mission of awakening the adventurer in everyone. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fairness not only in hiring, but also in development, compensation, and promotion. Our goal is to build an inclusive community where every team member can show up authentically and thrive. Together, we win as one team. Come join us! onX Maps will never ask for credit card or SSN details during the initial application process. For your digital safety, apply only through our legitimate website at onXmaps.com onX does not sell any Personal Information, but we may transfer employment related records to our service providers or third parties that provide business services to onX or as required by law. As part of our interview process, your conversation may be recorded for documentation purposes to allow interviewers to focus fully on the discussion. Recordings are confidential and accessible only to authorized personnel. Please note, onX respects all applicable laws regarding recording consent, and you will have an opportunity to opt\-out if preferred.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Cloud
jobs.description: Zed is building tools for people who care deeply about making software. We’re looking for an experienced backend engineer to help build the cloud services behind Zed and Delta. The server\-side infrastructure powers many of Zed's core features: all AI connections go through this system, as do the collaboration primitives, in addition to cross\-cutting concerns like auth, billing and telemetry. We are currently rebuilding our backend from a single stateful server to a fully distributed system, and looking for someone to help lead this effort. Our cloud capabilities are growing faster than the team’s capacity to build them. We need someone who can become a trusted technical partner to the engineers already doing this work: shaping projects, writing code, making sound decisions, and sharing responsibility for the system in production. This is primarily a software engineering role. Most of your time will go toward building backend software, but you’ll also need to understand and help own the infrastructure it runs on. \#\# What you’ll work on The cloud team owns work spanning APIs, application logic, storage, asynchronous processing, deployment, and operations. Projects may include: * Building Cloud Runners that provide ephemeral compute for development work. * Evolving billing to support new products, pricing, and packaging. * Integrating with identity providers and developing authorization capabilities. * Building integrations that connect Zed and Delta to developers’ existing workflows. Some projects involve unfamiliar technical challenges. Others are straightforward capabilities that customers and the business need. We’re looking for someone who takes care with both and enjoys moving between different kinds of work as priorities evolve. Our cloud backend is built in Rust, including services compiled to WebAssembly and running on Cloudflare Workers. We use managed infrastructure to reduce operational work and invest in tests that exercise complete workflows across clients and services. \[Read more about how we’re building Zed Cloud](https://maxdeviant.com/posts/2025/head\-in\-the\-zed\-cloud/). \#\# What you’ll do * **Turn emerging needs into shipped capabilities.** Work with engineering and product partners to clarify problems, choose a practical scope, and carry projects through implementation, rollout, and operation. * **Share technical stewardship of the cloud system.** Develop the context and judgment to make consequential decisions, guide work, and become someone teammates can turn to without routing every question through the same person. * **Stay hands\-on.** Write and review code, investigate difficult bugs, and work through the details that make a service correct, maintainable, and reliable. * **Make deliberate trade\-offs.** Recognize when a focused solution is enough, when an investment will make future work easier, and when to leave something alone. * **Help others work independently.** Share context, give useful feedback, and improve the tests, interfaces, and documentation that support the team’s work. * **Own production behavior.** Participate in on\-call, respond to incidents, and address recurring problems in the software and infrastructure. As you become familiar with the system, you should be able to take on significant cloud work independently while keeping the right people involved. Success means both delivering your own projects and helping the team make good decisions without depending on any one engineer. \#\# What you’ll bring * **You’ve owned backend services from design through production and continued development.** You’ve made API and data\-model decisions, shipped changes to systems with active users, and handled failures and operational issues after launch—not just implemented isolated features. * **You’ve built and operated the cloud infrastructure behind your software.** Your work has included provisioning resources, configuring deployments and monitoring, and diagnosing production problems across application code and infrastructure. * **You’ve led projects that other engineers contributed to while writing code yourself.** You’ve clarified requirements, worked through design decisions and dependencies, and followed through on delivery. Teammates have trusted you to guide work without escalating every decision. * **You’ve worked across different kinds of backend problems.** You can point to times you took responsibility outside your usual area, learned what you needed, and delivered. You’re comfortable moving between new capabilities, integrations, and operational improvements as priorities change. * **You make technical decisions with the people affected by them.** You’ve worked with engineers and product partners to compare approaches, choose what to build now, and decide what to defer.
